event.description: Tie the two transformer blocks’ attention output projections while retaining independent QKV maps, feed-forward sublayers, shared no-offset normalizations, rank-4 tied tokens, factorized rank-3 positions, d=14, ff=19, and the 75000-step schedule.
event.proposal: Family: parameter tying. Retained incumbent is attempt-0056 with 2886 parameters at 99.310000%, a +0.310000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the most recent accepted result is attempt-0038, which tied corresponding LayerNorms across the two blocks (3073, 99.71%); the most recent failed result is attempt-0049, multi-query attention, an optimization failure; 9 prior parameter-tying macro attempts. The immediately preceding token-rank automation ended in a rank-3 optimization failure after 75000 steps, which establishes a token-subspace boundary but does not test inter-block attention sharing. Hypothesis: the post-attention mixing map may be reusable across the two serial stages even though attention routing and value formation require layer-specific QKV weights. This is a representational parameter-tying change, not scalar pruning: it shares only one 14x14 output map and removes 196 actual parameters (2886 to 2690), while retaining two self-attention applications and all QKV/FF transforms. It is more informative than the nearest untested cross-layer QKV tie because it first constrains the already-mixed attention output rather than the causal attention scores or values.
